justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modestly bullish baseline for what appears to be an asset trading around the 363–368 range. At the one-day horizon, I anchored close to the last observed price, assuming mean-reverting behavior over very short windows and limited new information arriving overnight. The slight upward drift in the one-week and one-month estimates reflects a mild positive trend assumption — the idea that momentum or fundamental support nudges prices incrementally higher over time, but not dramatically so. The one-month estimate of 368 implies only about a 1.2% gain from the one-day anchor, which is a deliberately conservative projection acknowledging that trend continuation is uncertain.

The confidence interval widths expand meaningfully as the horizon lengthens, which is a standard reflection of uncertainty compounding over time. At one day, the 90% interval spans roughly 19 points, capturing normal daily volatility. By one month, the interval widens to 72 points, acknowledging that over four weeks, macro surprises, earnings, sentiment shifts, or technical breakdowns can accumulate in ways that are difficult to anticipate. The asymmetry between the intervals is relatively modest, suggesting I didn't have strong reason to weight tail risks heavily in either direction at the time of the forecast.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside these intervals include sudden macroeconomic shocks — unexpected central bank decisions, inflation data surprises, or geopolitical escalation — any of which could produce moves well beyond the stated bounds, particularly at the one-month horizon. On the upside, a risk-on catalyst such as stronger-than-expected economic data or positive earnings surprises could push prices above 404. On the downside, a broad market selloff, liquidity event, or sector-specific bad news could easily breach the 332 lower bound. These tail events, while individually low probability, collectively represent a meaningful chance of the realized outcome falling outside my stated 90% interval, as any such interval by definition excludes roughly 10% of scenarios by design.
